🖥 Iran, Oman and Uzbekistan discuss maritime freedom and transit cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The foreign ministers of Iran, Oman and Uzbekistan have discussed ways to strengthen transit cooperation linking Central Asia to regional waterways and stressed the importance of restoring freedom of navigation and ensuring safe maritime passage for international trade.

The trilateral meeting was held in Muscat on Tuesday, with Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov attending, according to a statement by Oman’s Foreign Ministry.
​
The three foreign ministers reviewed historical and brotherly relations between their countries and explored ways to expand bilateral and multilateral cooperation in political, economic, trade, investment and cultural fields. They also highlighted the importance of strategic partnerships in promoting sustainable development and serving the mutual interests of the three nations.
​
The talks focused on activating cooperation in transportation, land transit and logistics services to improve connectivity between Central Asia and the coastal countries of the Middle East.
​
The proposed cooperation aims to facilitate the movement of goods, encourage investment and strengthen economic and logistical integration across the region, the Omani Foreign Ministry said.
​
The foreign ministers also exchanged views on the latest regional developments, stressing the need to address crises through peaceful means, dialogue and negotiations to safeguard security, stability and mutual trust.
​
They emphasized respect for international law in addressing regional and international challenges and underscored the importance of restoring freedom of navigation and ensuring safe passage for international trade and import and export operations.
​
Such measures were highlighted as essential to supporting market stability and regional and international trade integration.
​
The meeting concluded with an emphasis on continued consultations and coordination among regional countries and stronger collective cooperation mechanisms based on mutual respect and respect for national sovereignty.
​
Araghchi, who is visiting Oman on an official trip, also held separate meetings with Al Busaidi and Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said on Tuesday morning.
